common: The immutable compiler contract controls semantics, buffer bindings, types, dispatch and legal workgroups.

Respect storage_dtype and every typed ABI binding: half, bfloat and float are distinct. Accumulate reductions in fp32. Round at the storage boundaries specified in semantics; RoPE constants stay fp32. Never reinterpret ushort as native bfloat arithmetic.
Use valid Metal Shading Language. Never call get_thread_execution_width() or get_num_threads_per_grid(). Thread/group indices must use the parameters allowed by contract.dispatch.
Host dispatch is fixed. Read whether one work item maps to a grid thread or a whole threadgroup. All group reduction barriers must be reached uniformly by the participating threads.
Read previous_attempts and compiler_feedback from this request; remote conversation memory is unnecessary.
For performance failures preserve the working ABI and correctness, and change a concrete implementation strategy. Small dispatches may have little headroom over a fused template.

silu_mul: Compute sigmoid in fp32 and multiply SiLU(input0) by input1; preserve operation semantics.
Keep both input buffers active in reflection and use the uint work-item count for bounds.
Coalesced elementwise loads and stores are the starting point. Threadgroup memory or barriers usually add overhead for this independent operation.
rope: Rotate query and key into two distinct output buffers, preserving both in the reflected ABI.
Use interleaved even/odd pairs, not a split-half rotation. Load both components before computing either rotated component.
Cosine and sine are already expanded per flattened pair in head-major order for this contract; do not infer a new position offset.
One work item owns one pair in each output. Reuse cosine and sine between query and key, with no threadgroup communication.
decoder_gemv_64_64: Decode M=1: the weight matrix is contiguous row-major [N,K]. One threadgroup owns one output feature and reduces K input products.
Use the declared group and tid attributes. Stride the K reduction by the selected workgroup_size (this is the group width, not SIMD width). Initialize inactive lanes to zero.
For a 32-thread workgroup, simd_sum is a legal optional reduction. For 64 or 128 threads, use the uniform threadgroup reduction and never assume a SIMD width.
Use uniform threadgroup barriers for shared reductions; only a designated thread writes the completed output.
The performance baseline includes scalar Linear and tuned vector-width 1/4 GEMV candidates. Preserve fp32 accumulation and numerical tolerance.

decoder_rope: Use position=valid_length[0]-1 from the read-only int buffer. Cosine/sine are full [32,8] tables, not pre-expanded pairs.
Q and K inputs [1,1,64] and outputs [1,4,1,16] have identical flattened order for this decode-only batch=1 contract. Preserve interleaved pairs.
One grid thread owns one pair of both outputs. Reuse table values between Q and K. The baseline is the two existing Q/K kernels in one command buffer.
decoder_residual_rmsnorm: Produce both the fp32 residual sum and its weighted RMSNorm output; the residual is used later by the decoder.
One threadgroup owns the width-64 row. Sum residual+update first, reduce squares, add epsilon=1e-5 after division by width.
Use group-uniform barriers. Do not read a global output written by another thread without the necessary synchronization; prefer threadgroup storage for the reduction.
The baseline is existing Add followed by RMSNorm in one command buffer.
decoder_gated_mlp: Fuse gate and up GEMVs with SiLU(gate)*up. Down projection remains a separate decoder GEMV.
One threadgroup owns one intermediate output feature. Reuse input loads for both projections; separately reduce gate and up sums.
Apply SiLU only after the entire gate dot product has been reduced. Multiply by the completed up dot product, not partial lane products.
Compare against two tuned template GEMVs plus SiLU*Mul in one command buffer.
